correctness.rationale: The proof is uniform for n>=4 and every prime-power q: translate to d, classify tau(d)=0,1,2,>=3. For tau=2 each ordered vertex-pair cover gives precisely one nonempty affine q-line. Intersections of two lines share their first or second index unless F is a two-edge matching; in the generic case there are exactly 2h pairwise coincidences and no triple concurrence, whereas matching yields two disjoint four-line pencils. These give \(2qc-2h+2m\); tau-one exceptions and ball volume are treated separately. Exhaustive support tests for n<=5 and deterministic larger ones totaled 36,504 and returned VERIFY_OK; experiments are not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The complete relevant 2026 primary manuscript was inspected in its ball-volume and star-intersection sections, not merely by abstract. It computes single-ball volume and unshifted star intersections, whereas the claimed second-order two-center profile depends on affine consistency and supported-edge matching corrections. value.rationale: The complete two-center ball intersection invariant is a natural nontrivial second-order refinement of the exact one-center volumes developed in the September 2026 work. It reveals stark non-distance-regularity and a sharp structural exception: tau=2 overlaps are only \(O(q)\) independently of n whereas tau=1 overlaps are \(\Theta(q^n)\). These exact figures can inform intersection-based packing and second-moment analyses; no downstream numerical improvement is asserted. The theorem treats every q,n and all support patterns, so it is not an arbitrary tiny parameter slice or table recomputation.
